studies.title: Classical rotor spreading and equilibrium comparison
studies.description: Grouped late-time summaries compare four ring sizes, three packet-energy scales and fixed-packet versus fixed-density preparation. At packet energy 10, the hot-pair fraction follows the microcanonical value 2/N and equilibrium-region residence is 87.2–90.4%. At packet energy 100, the hot pair retains 98.7–99.0% of local energy through t=2000.
studies.limits: Classical I=1 nearest-neighbor rings, equal-and-opposite initial hot pair, three related orientation seeds, and finite observation windows. The fixed-density series raises the initial packet energy with N; N=8 cases overlap between preparations. Late-time trapping is not permanent localization, and no quantum rotor evolution is included.

studies.title: Candidate geometric Hamiltonians and prepared-FL dynamics
studies.description: Exact K=4, total-spin-zero study (dimension 105). The baseline is complete-graph face-to-face area exchange plus on-site repulsion, with equal hopping strength on each bond. We added the positive RS-volume term and the signed triple-grasp term as separate candidate Hamiltonians, then evolved five explicitly prepared FL references under the baseline and both signed couplings. The 62 parameter settings cover U/t=0,1,5,20 and normalized coupling alpha=-2,-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1,2; the ring is included only as a sparse-hopping control. The study contains 6,510 saved energy levels and 50 prepared-state trajectories.
studies.limits: The complete graph represents tetrahedral face adjacency; the ring is a hopping control, not a proposed tetrahedron. The positive-volume and signed-grasp additions are tested candidate models, not derived physical interactions. Results use one copy, fixed K=4, project-normalized volume, and t=1; no physical coupling calibration or phase-transition claim is implied. The long-time dynamics are exact energy-basis samples with adaptive logarithmic coverage, not a uniformly resolved trace of every fast oscillation. Large thermal and dynamics CSVs are gzip-compressed for download; their source and package checksums are both listed.
studies.status: 62 Hamiltonian parameter settings and 50 FL trajectories calculated; 1,510 independent checks passed (maximum residual 1.07e-12)

studies.title: Four-site Hamiltonian spectra and RS-volume observables
studies.description: Exact diagonalization of the hopping-plus-on-site-repulsion operator H_G=-t Σ_(i,j)∈E_G(E_ij+E_ji)+(U/2)Σ_i n_i(n_i−1), where E_ij=a_i†a_j+b_i†b_j and n_i=a_i†a_i+b_i†b_i. Four sites, fixed boson number 2K and total spin zero; K=2,3,4 gives dimensions 20,50,105, with empty sites allowed. Compare the complete graph (6 hopping bonds) and periodic ring (4), with equal t per bond. The 30 cases use (t,U)=(0,1) or t=1 and U/t=0,1,5,20.
studies.limits: The positive Rovelli–Smolin (RS) volume V=(γℏ)^(3/2)Σ_(connected triples)√|q_ijk|, q_ijk=i[J_i·J_j,J_j·J_k], is a separate observable evaluated on energy eigenstates and Gibbs states; it is not a term in H_G, and no g_V V coupling was calculated. The optional spin-exchange setting is g=0. Both graphs select the same four connected triples, so V is the same operator and only the hopping graph changes. Project-normalized volume; physical calibration is open. The temperature response is a finite-sector crossover, not a phase transition. Ground-state entropy uses the Gibbs mixture when degenerate.
